assessment.reason: The projection sits right at 1.5 shots with a median of one. The model's fair price of about -130 clears the +115 offer, and even the upside stress case stays above break-even. No sourced fact clearly breaks the case, though Montréal's absences could raise his usage.
assessment.model_case: The projected mean is essentially on the line, so the under leans on a right-skewed count distribution rather than a low-volume forecast. The case rests on 23.2 projected minutes. If injuries push his minutes or power-play shot share higher, the margin narrows quickly, though the +10 production stress still clears break-even.
assessment.price_case: This is the standard 1.5 line at +115, which needs roughly a 46-in-100 hit rate. Three other books price the over as the slight favorite. The modest-weight blend sits only slightly above break-even, so the edge is thin and unvalidated.
assessment.context_case: The injury table lists several Montréal absences, including a defenseman, which could shift Hutson's deployment. Whether the projection already reflects that is unknown. A stale Shesterkin row conflicts with the goalie assumption, but the goalie matters little for shot volume.

qualitative_review.countercase: With Matheson and several Montréal forwards listed out, Hutson may log heavier minutes and a bigger power-play role than the 23.2-minute projection assumes. A mean already at 1.5 leaves little room for added volume. Books collectively shading toward the over may reflect that usage. The model is experimental, and the gap to market is moderate rather than trivial.
open_checks: Reconfirm the +115 price and the 1.5 line at BetMGM.
Check morning-skate pairings and power-play units for Hutson's usage with Matheson out.
Verify BetMGM settlement rules for player participation and overtime.

evidence.interpretation: If Matheson is out, Hutson may absorb extra minutes or power-play time. That would push shot volume above the projection and work against the under.
The listed return date has passed and the row is old, so it conflicts with the model's small Shesterkin share. Goalie identity likely matters little for a shot prop.

assessment.reason: At -200 the under needs about a two-in-three hit rate. The blended view barely clears that bar. Utah's thin center depth could promote Yamamoto into a bigger role, so the projection's 13.9 minutes is unconfirmed.
assessment.model_case: The projected assist mean of about 0.29 on 13.9 minutes supports a likely under. The weakness is opportunity: a move up the lineup or onto the power play would lift assist chances. The small stress band does not capture a role change.
assessment.price_case: This is the 0.5 line at -200, needing about a two-in-three win rate. The model's fair price is about -300. Only one other book is available, so consensus is thin, and the blend sits barely above break-even. A likely under can still be an unattractive price.
assessment.context_case: Cooley is listed day-to-day, with other Utah forwards out. His status could change Yamamoto's line placement. The snapshot is not game-day clearance.
blocking_checks: Cooley's status and Utah's line combinations: if Yamamoto moves into a top-six or power-play role, assist chances rise and the thin margin at -200 may vanish.

qualitative_review.countercase: Utah is missing Schmaltz and Guenther, and Cooley is uncertain, which could push Yamamoto into more minutes with better linemates. Heavy juice means one assist erases several wins. Limited book coverage weakens any claim that the market is mispriced.

findings.note: In a Nov. 13 odds update, Hutson moved past Cale Makar into third on the Norris Trophy board at +600. That points to a strong, healthy start to the season, which is mildly against an Under, but the page has no shot data.
ESPN's career stats page lists Hutson as active, with 3 goals, 7 assists and 10 points in 2026-27. The excerpt has no shots-on-goal or ice-time numbers, so it says nothing about the 1.5 line.

This older NHL.com piece describes Hutson as a pass-first defenseman who tied the rookie record for assists by a defenseman with 60. That fits a lower shot volume, but it does not cover this season or this game.

Nov 1, 2026: ruled out with an upper-body injury, day-to-day. I found no newer update, so his status for Nov 16 is unknown. He has 3 goals and 7 points (so 4 assists) in 9 games while playing on the third line, a pace that goes against the Under.

Last season he had 10 assists in 59 games on about 11:47 of ice time a night, a low assist rate. But this page's game log shows him getting an assist in each of three straight games from Oct 10 to Oct 15, 2026.
RotoWire expects Yamamoto to move between Utah's bottom-six lines this season but still get a fair number of scoring chances. That points to limited ice time and probably little power-play work.
